text: After 2-3 scans show zero open ports on a host, stop scanning it directly. It's likely behind another network segment requiring pivoting (SSH tunnel/proxy) through a reachable adjacent host.
When exec_in_kali denies reading a file as 'settled' (read 3x), use sha256sum or stat to check freshness instead of re-reading content.
Home-lab quests often require filling out a report template. Check for it early, verify it's not empty, and fill it before final submission.
Avoid heredocs with special characters for file writes via exec channel — they trigger 'Wide character' QEMU agent errors. Use simple echo/printf commands or base64 encoding instead.
When nmap shows no open ports, try direct service probes (curl http://host) first. Some hosts filter nmap's SYN scans but respond to actual HTTP/SMB requests.
Spawn parallel workers to enumerate services on different host groups simultaneously in large segments. Monitor status; individual worker failures shouldn't block overall progress.
Read SSH banners and MOTD carefully before guessing credentials — beginner targets often include valid usernames/passwords or hints in the login banner text.
When SSH login fails with common users (root, nobody, admin), re-check the service banner — it often specifies valid accounts rather than requiring brute force.

If HTTP directory listing is enabled, enumerate exposed files for credentials or configuration. Look for names like 'credentials.txt', 'config.php', or 'backup.zip' that reveal initial access vectors.
Exposed text files on beginner targets frequently contain temporary or default credentials marked with 'TODO' or 'temporary'. Read these immediately for quick SSH login without brute forcing.
SUID python3 shell via os.execl('/bin/sh') often hangs waiting for TTY. Use os.setuid(0); os.system('sh -i') or spawn shell via subprocess instead for reliable root shells.
When HTTP directory listing or gobuster fails, try common backup paths like /backup/, /old/, /tmp/ directly with curl. These often contain sensitive files or flags on beginner targets.
MySQL connections may fail with TLS errors if the server doesn't support SSL. Use --ssl-mode=DISABLED or -o ssl_mode=PREFERRED to connect without encryption.
Enumerate SMB shares anonymously first (smbclient -L //host/ -N) to discover share names. Restricted shares like 'finance' or 'hr' often appear in listings even when unreadable without credentials.
Read all text files in public SMB shares before abandoning restricted share access - runbooks, configs, and READMEs frequently contain service account credentials for other shares.
When nmap shows port 21 open, try anonymous FTP login immediately and check pub/ directory - beginner targets often place flags or credential files there without requiring authentication.
After anonymous SMB share enumeration, attempt to read each listed share - departmental shares like 'it' are often world-readable and contain credential files for SSH access.
Copy remote logs to local /tmp/ before parsing with grep/awk/sort. Avoids repeated SSH calls and enables efficient multi-pass analysis of large log files.
Parse /var/log/auth.log for 'Failed password' entries to identify SSH brute-force targets. Extract usernames with awk to find accounts under attack or valid users being tried.
When extracting values from JSON API responses in bash, use jq instead of tr/grep/cut string manipulation. jq handles arrays and nested objects reliably.
When a bash script exits with error but produces no output, run it with 'bash -x' to trace execution. This reveals where variables become empty or commands fail silently.
Check .bash_history of compromised users to reconstruct attacker actions. History reveals download URLs, stash directories, and persistence setup commands.
List /etc/cron.d/ with ls -la to find hidden dotfile crontabs. Attackers use names like .sysupdate for persistence that regular ls misses.
When tshark protocol filters fail on pcap analysis, use `strings capture.pcap | grep -iE 'pass|user|login'` to extract credentials and text notes directly from the capture without protocol parsing.
Root flags aren't always in /root/ - check unusual persistence locations mentioned in attacker notes like /var/tmp/.apt-cache/, /var/lib/.fonts-cache/, or other hidden directories.
When submitting forms to CSRF-protected apps, extract the hidden user_token from each page's HTML before POSTing. Use grep -oP to pull the token from the form field.
Local file inclusion path traversal often requires more directory levels than expected. If ../../../../ fails, try ../../../../../ (5 levels). Web root depth varies by installation.
When downloading exposed .git directories, wget -r often produces flat/malformed structure. Use git clone http://host/.git/ or download HEAD, refs/, objects/ individually to reconstruct the repo.
After multiple re-reads of the same directory with no new info, stop and try a fundamentally different approach rather than repeating the same failed command.
